# Template: argument_map
An informal-logic argument map: a conclusion box at the top, its premises in a row below with arrows of support (plain arrowhead) or objection (bar head, in the demand color) pointing up at it or at another premise. Choose this scene for ANY request about an argument map, premises and a conclusion, informal logic, modus ponens/tollens, or mapping out the structure of a reasoned argument or debate.
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "conclusion": {
   "type": "string",
   "description": "REQUIRED. The argument's conclusion."
  },
  "premises": {
   "type": "array",
   "minItems": 1,
   "maxItems": 5,
   "items": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
     "text": {
      "type": "string"
     },
     "supports": {
      "description": "What this premise supports: another premise's index, or \"conclusion\" (default)."
     },
     "objection": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Draw this link as an objection (bar head, demand color) instead of support (default false)."
     }
    },
    "required": [
     "text"
    ]
   }
  },
  "title": {
   "type": "string"
  }
 },
 "required": [
  "conclusion"
 ]
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- conclusion_box: the conclusion's box
- conclusion_text_<line>: its wrapped text lines
- premise_<i>: premises[i]'s box, with its wrapped text lines
- link_<i>: the arrow from premises[i] to its target
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Draw a modus ponens argument map: if it rains the ground gets wet, and it is raining, so the ground is wet." → params: {"conclusion":"The ground is wet.","premises":[{"text":"If it rains, the ground gets wet."},{"text":"It is raining."}]}

In YAML: `template: argument_map` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
